System Architecture Overview

Decoupled Identity Control Plane and Cryptographic Engine

VeriFile employs a decoupled architecture separating the Next.js identity issuer platform from a native Rust cryptographic signer for strict private key isolation.

01 · WEB

Web Control Plane (Next.js)

The issuer's frontend and API layer for modeling standards-compliant schemas, managing DID pair requests, and offering public endpoints for verification.

  • No-code schema builder with live JSON preview
  • Dashboard search, status filters, and pagination
  • IPFS schemas and two public PDF verification modes
Create schemaJSON preview
02 · SIGNER

Cryptographic Engine (Native PQC)

The isolated execution environment leveraging ssi_pq_core.node to sign payloads via ML-DSA and encrypt envelopes using ML-KEM + AES-256-GCM.

  • Encrypted SQLite wallet and local key custody
  • Real ML-DSA signing and ML-KEM/AES encryption
  • Proof of possession plus HMAC machine authentication
node lib/generate-pending-pdfs.js

CURRENT STATE

The web interface is functional today. The mobile UI is still being built; its cryptographic behavior is validated end to end by the scripts in lib/, the encrypted mobile_wallet.db, and the native ssi_pq_core.node module.

Credential lifecycle

From a schema to a verifiable PDF.

The framework connects issuer, signer, holder, and verifier in one understandable flow.

01

Design the schema

Create a VC schema with the no-code field builder, inspect its live JSON preview, and optionally publish the template through IPFS.

02

Issue and sign

Enter holder data in the web platform. The signer retrieves the pending request, proves key possession, and applies the ML-DSA signature.

03

Deliver privately

The signed credential is embedded in a PDF and encrypted with ML-KEM and AES-256-GCM for delivery to the holder.

04

Present and verify

A verifier checks proof of issuance by hash or performs full cryptographic validation of the signed PDF.

Security and privacy

Built around control, not collection.

VeriFile combines SSI principles with modern cryptography and deliberate data minimization.

PQ

Post-quantum cryptography

NIST-standardized ML-DSA signatures and ML-KEM key encapsulation protect authenticity and exchange.

K

Knowledge on demand

Personally identifiable information remains server-side only while a credential is awaiting signature and first download.

#

Content-free proof of issuance

Hash-based verification can confirm issuance and integrity without disclosing the credential's sensitive fields.

PoP

Defense in depth

Signer-to-platform communication combines a temporary ML-DSA credential with HMAC-based machine authorization.

Privacy by design

Sensitive data has an exit path.

After the first download, the platform deletes the holder's personally identifiable information and temporary credential files, retaining only anonymous evidence needed for validation.

Before signaturePII temporarily available
After first downloadPII permanently deleted
Retained evidenceDIDs · hashes · timestamps

Architecture

Issuer, holder, and verifier remain clearly separated.

The platform mediates the lifecycle while credentials remain portable and the signer preserves exclusive control of private keys.

Interactive performance. Measured trade-offs.
